title: For the First Time, This Dazzling San Francisco Snake is Being Released Into the Wild - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyFor the First Time, This Dazzling San Francisco Snake is Being Released Into the WildThe survival of the species depends on itDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CST on November 19, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe distinctive-looking San Francisco garter snake (Thamnophis sirtalis tetrataenia) lives a perilous existence. Only a few thousand remain across San Mateo and Santa Cruz, and the species has been on the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s endangered list since 1967 (the year the list originated).Powered By 10 ShareNextStayBut there’s new hope for the long-term survival of the species after 62 snakes were released into the wild from the San Francisco Zoo. It’s the first time that San Francisco garter snakes bred in captivity have been placed back into their natural habitat. The hope is that the reptiles will become self-sustaining.Read more: “This Snake’s Tail Has a Fake ‘Spider’ at the Tip”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
